issues.legal_issue: Residents are not entitled to a hearing before general legislative notifications alter a local body's territorial area when the governing law provides no hearing, unless the action is directed at an individual residence.
material_facts: The government issued notifications altering the territorial area of an existing local body and establishing a new local body for the altered area.
The governing law did not provide residents with an opportunity to be heard before the area was altered or the new body established.
The action affected residents as a group and was not directed at an individual resident's house.
issues.conclusion: No hearing was required before the notifications were issued in these circumstances; a different result may follow if an individual house is specifically being moved from one local body to another.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 3 and 4 of the Punjab Panchayati Raj Act, 1994, declarations defining a local body's area and establishing that body are legislative in character. Legislative acts are generally not subject to natural justice requirements unless the enactment provides for a hearing. The Court relied on Rameshchandra Kachardas Porwal v. State of Maharashtra and Union of India v. Cynamide India Ltd. It distinguished action directed at an individual's house, for which natural justice must be observed.

rule.if: challenge_to_local_body_notifications and notifications_reorganize_area_generally and governing_law_has_no_hearing_requirement and residents_affected_as_group and not individual_home_targeted

predicates.challenge_to_local_body_notifications: A party brought a proceeding challenging notifications concerning the territorial area or establishment of a local body.
predicates.notifications_reorganize_area_generally: The government issued notifications that generally changed the area of a local body or established a body for an area.
predicates.governing_law_has_no_hearing_requirement: The law governing the notifications did not provide for a hearing before the area was changed or the body established.
predicates.residents_affected_as_group: The notifications affected residents as a group rather than addressing a particular resident individually.
predicates.individual_home_targeted: The government specifically sought to move an individual resident's house from one local body to another.

issues.definition: When a challenge concerns general notifications affecting residents as a group, the law provides no hearing, and no individual home is targeted, a hearing is not required.

issues.legal_issue: Notifications defining a local body's territorial area and establishing the body may be issued simultaneously when the governing law requires no prior hearing.
material_facts: The government issued notifications defining the territorial area of a new local body and establishing that body on the same date.
The governing law did not require residents to be heard before those notifications were issued.
issues.conclusion: The notifications defining the area and establishing the local body could be issued simultaneously.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 3 and 4 of the Punjab Panchayati Raj Act, 1994 concern legislative acts, and the Act does not require a hearing before the declarations are made. The Court held that the High Court's contrary sequencing reasoning depended on its erroneous conclusion that a hearing was required.

predicates.challenge_to_local_body_notifications: A party brought a proceeding challenging notifications concerning the territorial area or establishment of a local body.
predicates.area_definition_and_body_establishment_n: The government issued the notification defining a local body's area and the notification establishing that body at the same time.
predicates.governing_law_has_no_hearing_requirement: The law governing the notifications did not require a hearing before the area was changed or the body established.

issues.definition: When a challenge concerns area-definition and body-establishment notifications issued together under a law that requires no hearing, issuing them simultaneously is permissible.

issues.legal_issue: Including a settlement in a local body's area satisfies the contiguity requirement where the settlement is partially contiguous to the village.
material_facts: A settlement was included in the territorial area of a new local body.
The settlement was partially, though not entirely, contiguous to the village with which the new local body was associated.
issues.conclusion: The partial contiguity amounted to substantial compliance with the statutory requirement, so the settlement could be included.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3(1) of the Punjab Panchayati Raj Act, 1994 provides for a Gram Sabha area consisting of a village or group of contiguous villages and addresses separate abadi areas. On examining the map, the Court found partial contiguity and held that there was substantial compliance with the statutory provision.

predicates.challenge_to_local_body_boundary_notific: A party brought a proceeding challenging the boundary notification for a local body.
predicates.included_settlement_partly_contiguous_to: The settlement included in the local body's area was partly contiguous to the village associated with that body.

issues.definition: When a boundary challenge concerns an included settlement that is partly contiguous to its associated village, the inclusion satisfies the contiguity requirement.
